signature_system.headline: Masonry Specified For Northeastern Pennsylvania Winters
signature_system.intro: Concrete and masonry in NEPA fail for a specific reason: freeze-thaw cycling. Water gets into a crack, freezes, expands, and the crack gets worse every winter until the whole surface fails. Everything we build is done with that in mind, not just to look good on install day.

blocks.title: Built to control cracking, not just hide it
blocks.body: A solid, compacted subbase, wire mesh or rebar, minimal water in the mix, and properly spaced control joints — sized at roughly a third of the concrete's depth and spaced at three times its thickness — let the material shrink and flex where we want it to instead of cracking at random.

blocks.title: Family craftsmanship, not a subcontracted crew
blocks.body: Joe started in masonry at 12 years old, apprenticing with his stepfather, then spent 8 years in the Bricklayers Union Local 5 before going out on his own in 1999. He and his crew do the work — nothing gets handed off to a subcontractor.

blocks.title: Sealed and finished to actually last
blocks.body: Sealing protects concrete from salt, acid, water and UV damage and helps prevent the staining and surface wear that most acids and de-icing salts cause over a Pennsylvania winter.

about_block.headline: 35+ Years In The Masonry Trade, Family Owned Since 1999
about_block.body: Joe Dougher Masonry Contractor is a family owned and operated masonry and concrete business serving Scranton, Clarks Summit, Dunmore, Old Forge and the surrounding NEPA area. Joe started in the trade at 12 years old, helping his stepfather Dave of Dave Jones Masonry, working summers and weekends through school. After graduation he worked with Jim Brunt Masonry, then Hudack Masonry Waterproofing, then spent 8 years in the Bricklayers Union Local 5 before going out on his own. Joe is a licensed (PA HIC #PA088400) and insured home improvement contractor with 35+ years in the field.

seo_body.headline: Masonry & Concrete Contractor In Scranton & Clarks Summit
paragraphs: Northeastern Pennsylvania is hard on concrete and masonry in a specific way: freeze-thaw cycling. Water works into any crack or joint, freezes, expands, and comes back the next winter to make it worse. A solid compacted subbase, correctly spaced control joints, wire mesh or rebar reinforcement, and sealing against water, salt and UV are what actually keep concrete and masonry sound through years of that cycle — not just at install.

We handle concrete driveways, sidewalks and patios, paver installations, structural and decorative retaining walls, stone, brick and stucco veneer, and custom fireplace and chimney masonry. Joe and his crew do the work themselves, priced fairly and explained in writing before anything starts.
If you're weighing a repair against a full replacement, or just want an honest read on what a project should cost, get us out to look. Estimates are free, and we'll tell you what we actually find.

faqs.q: How fast can I get an estimate?
faqs.a: Call or text (570) 815-3864. Joe comes out, looks at the job, and gives you a fair price up front — that's the thing clients mention most in their reviews.

faqs.q: Can I get a color, stain, or pattern in the concrete?
faqs.a: Yes — flat or textured finishes, stamped patterns, and custom color or stain options are all available. Ask about your own vision for the space.

faqs.q: How do you prevent concrete from cracking?
faqs.a: Concrete does crack, but it's controlled with a solid compacted subbase, wire mesh or rebar, minimal water in the mix, and properly spaced control joints so the material shrinks and flexes where it's supposed to instead of cracking at random.

faqs.q: How do you care for concrete after it's installed?
faqs.a: Concrete is durable and low-maintenance, but sealing protects it against salt, acid, water and UV damage — the things that actually deteriorate it over a Pennsylvania winter.

faqs.q: Will the concrete be perfectly smooth?
faqs.a: Concrete is not a manufactured product, so minor imperfections are normal — many clients are actually drawn to decorative concrete for that character.
